headline: High: next-ai-draw-io can exfiltrate or misuse shared document content via broad network/MCP, while awesome-nlp offers no isolation or runtime controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: next-ai-draw-io ingests PDFs, text, images, and draw.io content and uses natural-language commands plus MCP; if awesome-nlp content is copied into that workflow, prompt-like text could steer outputs. awesome-nlp itself has no runtime surfaces, so the bridge is one-way and indirect, but the shared content channel is plausible.
conditions: IF content from awesome-nlp is pasted or imported into next-ai-draw-io
IF next-ai-draw-io treats imported document text as instructions
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of untrusted text into next-ai-draw-io
Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from imported content
Review imported documents in read-only mode before AI processing
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported text

B_data_leakage.rationale: next-ai-draw-io has broad network egress and calls third-party model APIs, while awesome-nlp is a docs-only repo with no runtime egress. If shared files or prompts contain sensitive material, B can transmit it externally; A does not add a second leak path, but it also provides no containment.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are opened in next-ai-draw-io
IF next-ai-draw-io routes those contents to OpenAI, Anthropic, or another external API
mitigations: Turn off external model providers and use local-only inference
Avoid loading sensitive files into next-ai-draw-io
Rotate or redact secrets before processing
Restrict API keys to a test account
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on outbound prompts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-nlp is not runnable and exposes no write surfaces, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. next-ai-draw-io supports multiple instances and broad API access, but without a shared writable workspace or filesystem in A, the pairwise write-conflict pathway is weak.
conditions: IF both agents are attached to the same mutable workspace outside the provided profiles
IF next-ai-draw-io is configured to write to a shared directory
mitigations: Keep awesome-nlp as a reference-only repo
Assign separate working directories
Avoid concurrent edits to the same draw.io files
requires-engineering: add file locking around shared outputs

D_cascading_error.rationale: next-ai-draw-io can turn imported content into diagrams and AI-assisted outputs, so if awesome-nlp-derived text is treated as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect diagrams or downstream actions. A has no verification or action-taking role, and B's natural-language workflow increases the chance of unreviewed propagation.
conditions: IF outputs from awesome-nlp are used as source material in next-ai-draw-io
IF next-ai-draw-io renders or forwards those outputs without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before exporting diagrams
Cross-check generated facts against source documents
Use a checklist for citations and labels
Limit AI assistance to drafting, not final publication

E_compliance.rationale: next-ai-draw-io handles files and can send content to external model providers, creating a potential residency or retention mismatch for regulated documents. awesome-nlp is only a repository and does not itself process data, so the compliance risk is concentrated in B; A is cited to show the pair includes a non-processing component.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed through next-ai-draw-io
IF the selected provider stores or transfers data outside the required jurisdiction
mitigations: Use a provider with an approved DPA
Process only non-regulated documents
Disable retention where available
Log the chosen provider for each session
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing
